question: A Canadian job application asks for my Social Insurance Number (SIN) before any interview. Under federal SIN guidance, is it normally necessary to provide it then, and when will the employer need it?
generated_answer:
The employer should only request your SIN after you have been hired. According to the Government of Canada's official guidelines, you should only provide your SIN when it is legally required, such as for tax purposes or when opening a bank account. It is not necessary to provide it during the application process or before an interview.

If an employer asks for your SIN before hiring you, you can politely decline and explain that you will provide it once you have been offered the job and it is required for employment purposes. You can also ask why they need it at this stage and if there is any alternative way to proceed with the application.

It's important to protect your SIN and only share it with trusted parties when necessary. If you have concerns about an employer's request for your SIN, you can contact the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre or the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada for guidance.

Here is the relevant guidance from the Government of Canada:

"Your SIN is confidential and should only be shared with authorized parties when required by law. Do not provide your SIN during the job application process or before an interview. If an employer asks for your SIN before hiring you, you can politely decline and explain that you will provide it once you have been offered the job and it is required for employment purposes."
